passages.text: Then Pilate took Jesus and had Him flogged.
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate took Jesus.
Pilate ordered that Jesus be flogged.
The soldiers flogged Jesus.
passages.original: Τότε οὖν ἔλαβεν ὁ Πιλᾶτος τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἐμαστίγωσεν

passages.text: The soldiers twisted together a crown of thorns, set it on His head, and dressed Him in a purple robe.
passages.sermon:
Roman soldiers took Jesus.
They twisted a crown from thorns.
They placed the crown of thorns on Jesus’ head.
They put a purple robe on Jesus.
passages.original: καὶ οἱ στρατιῶται πλέξαντες στέφανον ἐξ ἀκανθῶν ἐπέθηκαν αὐτοῦ τῇ κεφαλῇ καὶ ἱμάτιον πορφυροῦν περιέβαλον αὐτόν

passages.text: And they went up to Him again and again, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!” and slapping Him in the face.
passages.sermon:
Roman soldiers approached Jesus many times.
They spoke to Jesus each time.
They said, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
They struck Jesus on the face.
passages.original: καὶ ἤρχοντο πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ ἔλεγον Χαῖρε ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ ἐδίδοσαν αὐτῷ ῥαπίσματα

passages.text: Once again Pilate came out and said to the Jews, “Look, I am bringing Him out to you to let you know that I find no basis for a charge against Him.”
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate came out again.
He spoke to the Jews.
He said, “Look, I am bringing Him out to you.”
He said, “I want you to know something.”
He said, “I find no basis for a charge against Him.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐξῆλθεν πάλιν ἔξω ὁ Πιλᾶτος καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Ἴδε ἄγω ὑμῖν αὐτὸν ἔξω ἵνα γνῶτε ὅτι οὐδεμίαν αἰτίαν εὑρίσκω ἐν αὐτῷ

passages.text: When Jesus came out wearing the crown of thorns and the purple robe, Pilate said to them, “Here is the man!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the man Pilate brought out to the crowd.
Jesus wore a crown made of thorns.
Jesus wore a purple robe.
Pilate spoke to the people.
Pilate said, “Here is the man!”
passages.original: ἐξῆλθεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἔξω φορῶν τὸν ἀκάνθινον στέφανον καὶ τὸ πορφυροῦν ἱμάτιον καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Ἰδοὺ ὁ ἄνθρωπος

passages.text: As soon as the chief priests and officers saw Him, they shouted, “Crucify Him! Crucify Him!” “You take Him and crucify Him,” Pilate replied, “for I find no basis for a charge against Him.”
passages.sermon:
The chief priests saw Jesus.
The officers saw Jesus.
They shouted loudly.
They said, “Crucify Him! Crucify Him!”
Pilate spoke to them.
Pilate said, “You take Him and crucify Him.”
Pilate said, “I find no basis for a charge against Him.”
passages.original: Ὅτε οὖν εἶδον αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ ὑπηρέται ἐκραύγασαν λέγοντες Σταύρωσον σταύρωσον Λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος Λάβετε αὐτὸν ὑμεῖς καὶ σταυρώσατε ἐγὼ γὰρ οὐχ εὑρίσκω ἐν αὐτῷ αἰτίαν

passages.text: “We have a law,” answered the Jews, “and according to that law He must die, because He declared Himself to be the Son of God.”
passages.sermon:
The Jews answered Pilate.
They said, “We have a law.”
According to our law, He must die.
He claimed to be the Son of God.
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι Ἡμεῖς νόμον ἔχομεν καὶ κατὰ τὸν νόμον ὀφείλει ἀποθανεῖν ὅτι Υἱὸν Θεοῦ ἑαυτὸν ἐποίησεν

passages.text: When Pilate heard this statement, he was even more afraid, and he went back into the Praetorium. “Where are You from?” he asked. But Jesus gave no answer.
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
The Jews told Pilate that Jesus claimed to be the Son of God.
Pilate heard this statement.
Pilate became even more afraid.
Pilate went back into the Praetorium.
Pilate spoke to Jesus.
Pilate asked Jesus, “Where are You from?”
Jesus did not answer Pilate.
passages.original: Ὅτε οὖν ἤκουσεν ὁ Πιλᾶτος τοῦτον τὸν λόγον μᾶλλον ἐφοβήθη καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸ πραιτώριον πάλιν καὶ λέγει τῷ Ἰησοῦ Πόθεν εἶ σύ Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἀπόκρισιν οὐκ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ

passages.text: So Pilate said to Him, “Do You refuse to speak to me? Do You not know that I have authority to release You and authority to crucify You?”
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate spoke to Jesus.
Pilate said, “You are not speaking to me.”
Pilate said, “Do you not know something?”
Pilate said, “I have authority to release you.”
Pilate said, “I have authority to crucify you.”
passages.original: Λέγει οὖν αὐτῷ ὁ Πιλᾶτος Ἐμοὶ οὐ λαλεῖς οὐκ οἶδας ὅτι ἐξουσίαν ἔχω ἀπολῦσαί σε καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἔχω σταυρῶσαί σε

passages.text: Jesus answered, “You would have no authority over Me if it were not given to you from above. Therefore the one who handed Me over to you is guilty of greater sin.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Pilate.
Jesus said, “You have no authority over Me by yourself.
God above gave you this authority.
Because of this, the person who handed Me over to you has committed a greater sin.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ Ἰησοῦς Οὐκ εἶχες ἐξουσίαν κατ’ ἐμοῦ οὐδεμίαν εἰ μὴ ἦν δεδομένον σοι ἄνωθεν διὰ τοῦτο ὁ παραδούς μέ σοι μείζονα ἁμαρτίαν ἔχει

passages.text: From then on, Pilate tried to release Him, but the Jews kept shouting, “If you release this man, you are no friend of Caesar. Anyone who declares himself a king is defying Caesar.”
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate tried to release Jesus.
The Jews kept shouting at Pilate.
They said, “If you release this man, you are not a friend of Caesar.”
They also said, “Anyone who makes himself a king opposes Caesar.”
passages.original: Ἐκ τούτου ὁ Πιλᾶτος ἐζήτει ἀπολῦσαι αὐτόν οἱ δὲ Ἰουδαῖοι ἐκραύγασαν λέγοντες Ἐὰν τοῦτον ἀπολύσῃς οὐκ εἶ φίλος τοῦ Καίσαρος πᾶς ὁ βασιλέα ἑαυτὸν ποιῶν ἀντιλέγει τῷ Καίσαρι

passages.text: When Pilate heard these words, he brought Jesus out and sat on the judgment seat at a place called the Stone Pavement, which in Hebrew is Gabbatha.
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate heard the words of the Jews.
Pilate brought Jesus outside.
Pilate sat down on the judgment seat.
The judgment seat was at a place called the Stone Pavement.
In Hebrew, people called this place Gabbatha.
passages.original: Ὁ οὖν Πιλᾶτος ἀκούσας τῶν λόγων τούτων ἤγαγεν ἔξω τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἐπὶ βήματος εἰς τόπον λεγόμενον Λιθόστρωτον Ἑβραϊστὶ δὲ Γαββαθα

passages.text: It was the day of Preparation for the Passover, about the sixth hour. And Pilate said to the Jews, “Here is your King!”
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
The Jews had brought Jesus to Pilate.
It was the day of Preparation for the Passover.
The time was about the sixth hour.
Pilate spoke to the Jews.
Pilate said, "Here is your King!"
passages.original: ἦν δὲ Παρασκευὴ τοῦ πάσχα ὥρα ἦν ὡς ἕκτη καὶ λέγει τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις Ἴδε ὁ Βασιλεὺς ὑμῶν

passages.text: At this, they shouted, “Away with Him! Away with Him! Crucify Him!” “Shall I crucify your King?” Pilate asked. “We have no king but Caesar,” replied the chief priests.
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Jesus stood before Pilate.
The Jewish crowd shouted loudly.
They said, “Take Him away! Take Him away! Crucify Him!”
Pilate spoke to the crowd.
He asked, “Shall I crucify your King?”
The chief priests answered Pilate.
They said, “We have no king except Caesar.”
passages.original: Ἐκραύγασαν οὖν Ἐκεῖνοι Ἆρον ἆρον σταύρωσον αὐτόν Λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος Τὸν Βασιλέα ὑμῶν σταυρώσω Ἀπεκρίθησαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς Οὐκ ἔχομεν βασιλέα εἰ μὴ Καίσαρα

passages.text: Then Pilate handed Jesus over to be crucified, and the soldiers took Him away.
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Jesus was a Jewish man.
Pilate handed Jesus over to the soldiers.
Pilate did this so that they would crucify Jesus.
The soldiers took Jesus away.
passages.original: Τότε οὖν παρέδωκεν αὐτὸν αὐτοῖς ἵνα σταυρωθῇ Παρέλαβον οὖν τὸν Ἰησοῦν

passages.text: Carrying His own cross, He went out to The Place of the Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.
passages.sermon:
Jesus carried His own cross.
He went out from the city.
He went to a place called The Place of the Skull.
In Hebrew, people call this place Golgotha.
passages.original: Καὶ βαστάζων ἑαυτῷ τὸν σταυρὸν ἐξῆλθεν εἰς τὸν λεγόμενον Κρανίου τόπον ὃ λέγεται Ἑβραϊστὶ Γολγοθᾶ

passages.text: There they crucified Him, and with Him two others, one on each side, with Jesus in the middle.
passages.sermon:
The soldiers crucified Jesus at Golgotha.
They crucified two other men with Him.
One man was on each side of Jesus.
Jesus was in the middle.
passages.original: ὅπου αὐτὸν ἐσταύρωσαν καὶ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ἄλλους δύο ἐντεῦθεν καὶ ἐντεῦθεν μέσον δὲ τὸν Ἰησοῦν

passages.text: Pilate also had a notice posted on the cross. It read: JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate wrote a notice.
Pilate placed the notice on the cross.
The notice said: JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
passages.original: Ἔγραψεν δὲ καὶ τίτλον ὁ Πιλᾶτος καὶ ἔθηκεν ἐπὶ τοῦ σταυροῦ ἦν δὲ γεγραμμένον ΙΗΣΟΥΣ Ο ΝΑΖΩΡΑΙΟΣ Ο ΒΑΣΙΛΕΥΣ ΤΩΝ ΙΟΥΔΑΙΩΝ

passages.text: Many of the Jews read this sign, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city, and it was written in Hebrew, Latin, and Greek.
passages.sermon:
Many Jews read this sign.
The place where Jesus was crucified was near the city.
The sign was written in Hebrew.
The sign was written in Latin.
The sign was written in Greek.
passages.original: Τοῦτον οὖν τὸν τίτλον πολλοὶ ἀνέγνωσαν τῶν Ἰουδαίων ὅτι ἐγγὺς ἦν ὁ τόπος τῆς πόλεως ὅπου ἐσταυρώθη ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἦν γεγραμμένον Ἑβραϊστί Ῥωμαϊστί Ἑλληνιστί

passages.text: So the chief priests of the Jews said to Pilate, “Do not write, ‘The King of the Jews,’ but only that He said, ‘I am the King of the Jews.’ ”
passages.sermon: The chief priests of the Jews spoke to Pilate.\r\nThey said, “Do not write, ‘The King of the Jews.’”\r\nThey said, “Write that this man said, ‘I am the King of the Jews.’”
passages.original: ἔλεγον οὖν τῷ Πιλάτῳ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς τῶν Ἰουδαίων Μὴ γράφε Ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἀλλ’ ὅτι ἐκεῖνος εἶπεν Βασιλεύς εἰμι τῶν Ἰουδαίων

passages.text: Pilate answered, “What I have written, I have written.”
passages.sermon: Pilate was the Roman governor.\r\nPilate answered the chief priests.\r\nPilate said, “What I have written, I have written.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη ὁ Πιλᾶτος Ὃ γέγραφα γέγραφα

passages.text: When the soldiers had crucified Jesus, they divided His garments into four parts, one for each soldier, with the tunic remaining. It was seamless, woven in one piece from top to bottom.
passages.sermon:
Roman soldiers crucified Jesus.
They took His garments.
They divided His garments into four parts.
Each soldier received one part.
One piece of clothing remained.
This piece was the tunic.
The tunic was seamless.
It was woven in one piece from top to bottom.
passages.original: Οἱ οὖν στρατιῶται ὅτε ἐσταύρωσαν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἔλαβον τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐποίησαν τέσσαρα μέρη ἑκάστῳ στρατιώτῃ μέρος καὶ τὸν χιτῶνα ἦν δὲ ὁ χιτὼν ἄραφος ἐκ τῶν ἄνωθεν ὑφαντὸς δι’ ὅλου

passages.text: So they said to one another, “Let us not tear it. Instead, let us cast lots to see who will get it.” This was to fulfill the Scripture: “They divided My garments among them, and cast lots for My clothing.” So that is what the soldiers did.
passages.sermon:
Roman soldiers crucified Jesus.
They took His garments.
They found His tunic was seamless.
The tunic was woven in one piece from top to bottom.
The soldiers spoke to each other.
They said, “Let us not tear the tunic.”
They said, “Let us cast lots to decide who will get it.”
They did this to fulfill Scripture.
The Scripture says, “They divided My garments among them.”
The Scripture says, “They cast lots for My clothing.”
The soldiers did these things.
passages.original: εἶπαν οὖν πρὸς ἀλλήλους Μὴ σχίσωμεν αὐτόν ἀλλὰ λάχωμεν περὶ αὐτοῦ τίνος ἔσται ἵνα ἡ γραφὴ πληρωθῇ ἡ λέγουσα Διεμερίσαντο τὰ ἱμάτιά μου ἑαυτοῖς καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν ἱματισμόν μου ἔβαλον κλῆρον Οἱ μὲν οὖν στρατιῶται ταῦτα ἐποίησαν

passages.text: Near the cross of Jesus stood His mother and her sister, as well as Mary the wife of Clopas and Mary Magdalene.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was crucified.
His cross stood on a hill.
His mother stood near the cross.
Her sister stood with her.
Mary, the wife of Clopas, stood there too.
Mary Magdalene also stood near the cross.
passages.original: Εἱστήκεισαν δὲ παρὰ τῷ σταυρῷ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἡ ἀδελφὴ τῆς μητρὸς αὐτοῦ Μαρία ἡ τοῦ Κλωπᾶ καὶ Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνή

passages.text: When Jesus saw His mother and the disciple whom He loved standing nearby, He said to His mother, “Woman, here is your son.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was on the cross.
His mother stood near Him.
The disciple whom Jesus loved stood nearby.
Jesus saw His mother.
Jesus saw the beloved disciple standing close.
Jesus spoke to His mother.
Jesus said, “Woman, here is your son.”
passages.original: Ἰησοῦς οὖν ἰδὼν τὴν μητέρα καὶ τὸν μαθητὴν παρεστῶτα ὃν ἠγάπα λέγει τῇ μητρί Γύναι ἴδε ὁ υἱός σου

passages.text: Then He said to the disciple, “Here is your mother.” So from that hour, this disciple took her into his home.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the disciple whom He loved.\r\nHe said, "Here is your mother."\r\nFrom that hour, the disciple took Mary, the mother of Jesus, into his own home.
passages.original: εἶτα λέγει τῷ μαθητῇ Ἴδε ἡ μήτηρ σου καὶ ἀπ’ ἐκείνης τῆς ὥρας ἔλαβεν ὁ μαθητὴς αὐτὴν εἰς τὰ ἴδια

passages.text: After this, knowing that everything had now been accomplished, and to fulfill the Scripture, Jesus said, “I am thirsty.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus hung on the cross.
He knew everything was now finished.
He understood that all things were accomplished.
He wanted to fulfill the Scripture.
Jesus said, “I am thirsty.”
passages.original: Μετὰ τοῦτο εἰδὼς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἤδη πάντα τετέλεσται ἵνα τελειωθῇ ἡ γραφὴ λέγει Διψῶ

passages.text: A jar of sour wine was sitting there. So they soaked a sponge in the wine, put it on a stalk of hyssop, and lifted it to His mouth.
passages.sermon:
A jar stood nearby.
The jar was full of sour wine.
They took a sponge.
They filled the sponge with the sour wine.
They put the sponge on a stalk of hyssop.
They lifted the sponge to Jesus’ mouth.
passages.original: σκεῦος ἔκειτο ὄξους μεστόν σπόγγον οὖν μεστὸν τοῦ ὄξους ὑσσώπῳ περιθέντες προσήνεγκαν αὐτοῦ τῷ στόματι

passages.text: When Jesus had received the sour wine, He said, “It is finished.” And bowing His head, He yielded up His spirit.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was on the cross.
He had just received the sour wine.
Jesus spoke.
He said, “It is finished.”
Jesus bowed His head.
He gave up His spirit.
Jesus died.
passages.original: ὅτε οὖν ἔλαβεν τὸ ὄξος ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Τετέλεσται καὶ κλίνας τὴν κεφαλὴν παρέδωκεν τὸ πνεῦμα

passages.text: It was the day of Preparation, and the next day was a High Sabbath. In order that the bodies would not remain on the cross during the Sabbath, the Jews asked Pilate to have the legs broken and the bodies removed.
passages.sermon:
The Jews wanted to follow their religious laws.
It was the day of Preparation.
The next day would be a High Sabbath.
The Jews did not want the bodies to remain on the cross during the Sabbath.
They went to Pilate.
They asked Pilate to have the legs of those crucified broken.
They also asked for the bodies to be removed.
passages.original: Οἱ οὖν Ἰουδαῖοι ἐπεὶ Παρασκευὴ ἦν ἵνα μὴ μείνῃ ἐπὶ τοῦ σταυροῦ τὰ σώματα ἐν τῷ σαββάτῳ ἦν γὰρ μεγάλη ἡ ἡμέρα ἐκείνου τοῦ σαββάτου ἠρώτησαν τὸν Πιλᾶτον ἵνα κατεαγῶσιν αὐτῶν τὰ σκέλη καὶ ἀρθῶσιν

passages.text: So the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first man who had been crucified with Jesus, and those of the other.
passages.sermon:
Roman soldiers came to the crosses.
They saw three men crucified.
Jesus was in the center.
Two other men were crucified with Him.
The soldiers broke the legs of the first man.
They also broke the legs of the other man crucified with Jesus.
passages.original: ἦλθον οὖν οἱ στρατιῶται καὶ τοῦ μὲν πρώτου κατέαξαν τὰ σκέλη καὶ τοῦ ἄλλου τοῦ συσταυρωθέντος αὐτῷ

passages.text: But when they came to Jesus and saw that He was already dead, they did not break His legs.
passages.sermon: The soldiers came to Jesus.\r\nThey saw Jesus was already dead.\r\nThey did not break Jesus’ legs.
passages.original: ἐπὶ δὲ τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐλθόντες ὡς εἶδον ἤδη αὐτὸν τεθνηκότα οὐ κατέαξαν αὐτοῦ τὰ σκέλη

passages.text: Instead, one of the soldiers pierced His side with a spear, and immediately blood and water flowed out.
passages.sermon:
One soldier stood near Jesus.
This soldier held a spear.
He pierced the side of Jesus with the spear.
Blood flowed out from Jesus’ side.
Water also flowed out from Jesus’ side.
This happened immediately after the soldier pierced Him.
passages.original: ἀλλ’ εἷς τῶν στρατιωτῶν λόγχῃ αὐτοῦ τὴν πλευρὰν ἔνυξεν καὶ ἐξῆλθεν εὐθὺς αἷμα καὶ ὕδωρ

passages.text: The one who saw it has testified to this, and his testimony is true. He knows that he is telling the truth, so that you also may believe.
passages.sermon:
A person saw these things happen.
This person has given a testimony about what he saw.
His testimony is true.
He knows that he is telling the truth.
He tells the truth so that you may also believe.
passages.original: καὶ ὁ ἑωρακὼς μεμαρτύρηκεν καὶ ἀληθινὴ αὐτοῦ ἐστιν ἡ μαρτυρία καὶ ἐκεῖνος οἶδεν ὅτι ἀληθῆ λέγει ἵνα καὶ ὑμεῖς πιστεύητε

passages.text: Now these things happened so that the Scripture would be fulfilled: “Not one of His bones will be broken.”
passages.sermon:
These things happened for a reason.
God wanted to fulfill the Scripture.
The Scripture says, “Not one of His bones will be broken.”
God made sure this prophecy came true.
Jesus’ bones were not broken.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο γὰρ ταῦτα ἵνα ἡ γραφὴ πληρωθῇ Ὀστοῦν οὐ συντριβήσεται αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And, as another Scripture says: “They will look on the One they have pierced.”
passages.sermon:
Another Scripture speaks about Jesus.
This Scripture says, “They will look on the One they have pierced.”
Jesus is the One they pierced.
People will look at Him.
passages.original: καὶ πάλιν ἑτέρα γραφὴ λέγει Ὄψονται εἰς ὃν ἐξεκέντησαν

passages.text: Afterward, Joseph of Arimathea, who was a disciple of Jesus (but secretly for fear of the Jews), asked Pilate to let him remove the body of Jesus. Pilate gave him permission, so he came and removed His body.
passages.sermon:
Joseph came from Arimathea.
Joseph was a disciple of Jesus.
Joseph followed Jesus in secret.
He hid because he feared the Jews.
After these things happened, Joseph went to Pilate.
Joseph asked Pilate for permission to take the body of Jesus.
Pilate gave Joseph permission.
Joseph went and took the body of Jesus.
passages.original: Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα ἠρώτησεν τὸν Πιλᾶτον Ἰωσὴφ ὁ ἀπὸ Ἁριμαθαίας ὢν μαθητὴς τοῦ Ἰησοῦ κεκρυμμένος δὲ διὰ τὸν φόβον τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἵνα ἄρῃ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ ἐπέτρεψεν ὁ Πιλᾶτος ἦλθεν οὖν καὶ ἦρεν τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Nicodemus, who had previously come to Jesus at night, also brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about seventy-five pounds.
passages.sermon:
Nicodemus came.
Nicodemus had visited Jesus before.
Nicodemus came to Jesus at night the first time.
Nicodemus brought a mixture.
The mixture was myrrh and aloes.
The mixture weighed about seventy-five pounds.
passages.original: ἦλθεν δὲ καὶ Νικόδημος ὁ ἐλθὼν πρὸς αὐτὸν νυκτὸς τὸ πρῶτον φέρων μίγμα σμύρνης καὶ ἀλόης ὡς λίτρας ἑκατόν

passages.text: So they took the body of Jesus and wrapped it in linen cloths with the spices, according to the Jewish burial custom.
passages.sermon:
Joseph of Arimathea was a disciple of Jesus.
He followed Jesus in secret because he feared the Jews.
Nicodemus had come to Jesus at night before.
Joseph and Nicodemus took the body of Jesus.
They wrapped the body in linen cloths.
They used spices with the linen cloths.
This was the Jewish custom for burial.
passages.original: ἔλαβον οὖν τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ ἔδησαν αὐτὸ ὀθονίοις μετὰ τῶν ἀρωμάτων καθὼς ἔθος ἐστὶν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ἐνταφιάζειν

passages.text: Now there was a garden in the place where Jesus was crucified, and in the garden a new tomb in which no one had yet been laid.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was crucified at a certain place.
There was a garden at that place.
In the garden, there was a new tomb.
No one had ever been placed in that tomb.
passages.original: Ἦν δὲ ἐν τῷ τόπῳ ὅπου ἐσταυρώθη κῆπος καὶ ἐν τῷ κήπῳ μνημεῖον καινόν ἐν ᾧ οὐδέπω οὐδεὶς ἦν τεθειμένος

passages.text: And because it was the Jewish day of Preparation and the tomb was nearby, they placed Jesus there.
passages.sermon:
The people took the body of Jesus.
It was the Jewish day of Preparation.
A tomb was nearby.
They placed Jesus in that tomb.
passages.original: ἐκεῖ οὖν διὰ τὴν Παρασκευὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων ὅτι ἐγγὺς ἦν τὸ μνημεῖον ἔθηκαν τὸν Ἰησοῦν
